subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should incompatible Docker hosts get an explicit dangerous `no-new-privileges` opt-out, an image/runtime compatibility fix, or diagnostic-only handling for now?
rationale: The bug is actionable, but restoring affected hosts may weaken Docker sandbox hardening or add a new config surface, and repository policy treats fallback/config/security-boundary changes as maintainer-owned decisions.

options.title: Explicit Audited Opt-Out
options.body: Add a default-on `no-new-privileges` setting only as a dangerous, well-documented override with config schema, dangerous-config reporting, docs, tests, and real Docker proof.

options.title: Runtime/Image Fix First
options.body: Investigate and fix the sandbox image or Docker/runtime interaction so the hardened flag keeps working without adding a security-weaker config option.

options.title: Diagnostics Only
options.body: Keep sandbox hardening unchanged and improve status/session/doctor diagnostics so affected operators understand the host-level failure and can choose an external mitigation.

recommendation.title: Explicit Audited Opt-Out
recommendation.body: Add a default-on `no-new-privileges` setting only as a dangerous, well-documented override with config schema, dangerous-config reporting, docs, tests, and real Docker proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent and historical footprint across the Docker sandbox create path, config validation, and security-sensitive sandbox policy files.
